clue.text: Interrupting performance, sailor with drink turned around and ran down

indicators.note: the reversed pair breaks into the word for a performance, splitting it in the middle

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance

indicators.note: the sailor and the drink, taken together, are read backwards

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A drunken sailor barges into a show and then gets disparaged for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned around' turns TARGIN into NIGRAT, which 'Interrupting' puts inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to belittle or disparage them, a close synonym.

clue.text: Hesitate, as one who was tickled to meet the Queen

indicators.note: the comedian's name meets the royal letters, one after the other

parts.note: Ken Dodd, the British comedian, made 'How tickled I am' his catchphrase and waved a tickling stick
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates like a nervous comedian about to meet the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a Liverpool comedian known for his tickling stick and 'tickled' catchphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter or move falteringly, much like wavering or faltering.

clue.text: Room with a Parisian sitting up in bed in India

indicators.note: in a down entry the room and the French article are read upwards

parts.note: a hall is a room
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman sitting up in bed in a room in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry river bed or ravine in India, an Anglo-Indian word.

clue.text: He had, having earlier understood scripture, to confront wickedness or become corrupt

indicators.note: understood and scripture come before the contraction
the contraction faces up to wickedness, which follows it

parts.note: to get something is to understand it, so got
OT is the Old Testament
he'd is short for he had
evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: A man who knew his scripture confronts evil.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for falling into ruin or moral decline.

clue.text: A style for home? No

parts.note: a way of doing something is its style

explanation.surface: Is there a design style for the home? No.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting match not played at home is played elsewhere, the opposite of home.

clue.text: Discarded vehicle floating on river outside the building

indicators.note: in a down entry the river comes below and the vehicle sits on top of it

parts.note: ex means former, discarded
a tram is a vehicle
the Ural is a river in Russia

explanation.surface: An old abandoned vehicle floats along a river by a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally beyond the walls; used of studies or activities outside a college or institution.

clue.text: A bird like this may be seen in Nile location

definitions.text: A bird like this may be seen in Nile location

parts.words: A bird like this may be seen in Nile location
parts.note: the letter A placed before this bird's name gives a city in Upper Egypt on the Nile, famous for its dam, so the bird is seen in the place name

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note that such a bird can be spotted somewhere along the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: Aswan is a city on the Nile in Egypt; the clue's 'A' plus the bird spells it, so the bird sits within the location's name rather than on its river.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the long-necked white waterfowl whose name, after an A, spells the Egyptian city.

clue.text: It's miserable, being married, having inner strain

indicators.note: the word for married holds the strain in its interior

parts.note: wed means married
to retch is to strain as if vomiting

explanation.surface: Married life is miserable when there is strain within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhappy and pitiable, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Sweet winner — dog that's lost its tail

parts.note: the winner is number one, NO I

indicators.note: the dog's name loses its final letter

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: A prize-winning dog has lost its tail, sweetly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut chocolate, a sweet; the word is French for little hazelnut.

clue.text: One north European 'into' poet — whose study is superficial?

indicators.note: the quoted word tells us the Latvian goes into the poet's name

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
one is the Roman numeral I
a Lett is a Latvian, from northern Europe

explanation.surface: A Baltic scholar who is 'into' a poet — but perhaps only skin-deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is set in quotes because it serves as the insertion signal, while its surface sense is a fan's enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler who takes up an art or subject without serious study is a classic amateur of that kind.

clue.text: African money is frozen, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for frozen is moved to the end

parts.note: iced means frozen

explanation.surface: A report that some African currency has been frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' takes the I from ICED to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the currency unit of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: Short story on e.g. Radio 4 generates controversy

indicators.note: in a down entry the short story sits on top of the broadcaster

parts.note: a conte is a short story, from French
BBC Radio 4 is an example of a radio station

explanation.surface: A short story broadcast on BBC Radio 4 stirs up controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio 4 is the BBC's main speech radio channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispute or argument, the act of contesting a matter.

clue.text: A court involved in measures for sanctions

indicators.note: the A and the court are wrapped inside the printers' measures

parts.note: ens are printers' measures of width

explanation.surface: A court is involved in measures concerning sanctions against someone.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of measure, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction a law is to pass or approve it, which is to make it law.

clue.text: That was painful, being in exposed carriage

indicators.note: the exclamation of pain sits inside the word for exposed

parts.note: bare means exposed
ouch is what one says when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone yelps at the pain of riding in an open carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood, popular in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Female associated with false image in party restricted by realists somehow

indicators.note: the party is held within the rearranged letters
the letters of realists are arranged in some other way

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party woman hemmed in by realists over a false image.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long descriptive phrase rather than one word: an idol is a false image, and the -ess ending marks the worshipper as female.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who worships an idol, a false image of a god.

clue.text: Women excluded in new trade? Further change needed!

indicators.note: the men-only phrase is placed inside the rearranged trade letters
a new version of the word trade has its letters rearranged

parts.note: with women excluded you have just men

explanation.surface: A call for further reform in a male-only profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the trade letters, and the men-only phrase is split into them after the fourth letter, rather than added at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: A readjustment is a further alteration, a modification made again.

clue.text: Current strength of politician beginning to erupt in a temper

indicators.note: the politician and the first letter go inside the phrase a rage

parts.note: a rage is a temper
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the beginning of erupt is its first letter

explanation.surface: A politician starting to erupt in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present'; it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The strength of an electric current, measured in amps.

clue.text: Smarter wooden frame that absorbs water

indicators.note: the frame takes the water into itself

parts.note: a bier is a frame for carrying a coffin
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A wooden frame that soaks up water is smarter.
explanation.definitionFit: More intelligent, the comparative of clever in a colloquial form.

clue.text: Real smile as I run around in country air

indicators.note: the letters run around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone smiling as they jog around, perhaps in the open countryside air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country air' looks like fresh rural air; it means a nation's tune.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French national anthem, a nation's song or tune.

clue.text: To develop biologically, little animal took food

parts.note: a pup is a young animal
ate means took food

explanation.surface: A young animal ate to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect larva becomes a chrysalis in this stage of its growth.

clue.text: Best achievement follows poor exam grades

indicators.note: the achievement comes after the poor grades

parts.note: D and E are poor exam grades
a feat is an achievement

explanation.surface: A top result following poor exam grades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective; it is the verb to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to beat them, overcoming them.

clue.text: Select group in English Literature is embracing someone really good

indicators.note: the word is wraps around the saint

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is someone really good

explanation.surface: An English Literature group that welcomes a star student.
explanation.definitionFit: People who think themselves superior form an exclusive circle, so a plural noun for snobbish insiders.

clue.text: A knight entertained by clever king

indicators.note: the A and the knight are held inside the word for clever

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight is hosted by a shrewd monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish ruler of England famed for the story of commanding the tide.

clue.text: Sound of very important little bird

indicators.note: the phrase is heard, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: very important is key and little is wee, giving 'key wee'

explanation.surface: The call of a tiny but important bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless bird of New Zealand.

clue.text: Fixed line needed when picking team

indicators.note: the word for when picks up, or takes in, the team

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A firm rule that applies whenever a team is being selected.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight line about which a body rotates or which a graph is drawn along.

clue.text: With lot gathered round, bring out toast

indicators.note: the word for one's lot is gathered round the word for bring out

parts.note: fate is one's lot in life
elicit means to draw or bring out

explanation.surface: Gathering everyone round before raising a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast someone is to congratulate or wish them well, which this formal verb means.

clue.text: Country's name as before, having gained independence

indicators.note: the old word for before takes the letter for independence into itself

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
I is a standard abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A nation keeps its old name after winning independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' looks like part of the definition, but 'before' gives ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Irish-language name of Ireland, also its official name from 1937.

clue.text: Duty to be done — a hint intended to be listened to

indicators.note: the phrase is meant to be heard, so we want a word sounding like it

parts.note: a hint is a sign and intended is meant, so this says 'a sign meant'

explanation.surface: A clue to a task that is meant to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A task allocated to someone, such as homework or a work job.
